description: Fixed synthetic, non-sensitive context-selection workload. Items are illustrative test records, not live provider or user evidence.

cases.query: provider successful probe rotation cursor next eligible state latency avoid retry same provider

items.content: The media service records request timestamps, provider identifiers, output metadata, and operational observations so an operator can audit a completed job.
A provider catalogue describes model identifiers, capabilities, eligibility, and general health observations. Catalogue records are not themselves a scheduling decision.

After a provider probe succeeds, choose the next eligible provider from the persisted rotation cursor. Do not immediately retry the same successful provider as the next probe. Record health state and latency.
Persist the cursor after each attempted provider. The next scheduled run begins at the next index, preventing repeated selection of the same provider when another eligible provider is due.

cases.query: latest verified quota renewal date reset window supersedes older estimate

items.content: Provider summaries may collect model limits, request-rate guidance, and links to usage dashboards. A summary should not replace a timestamped account observation.
An older estimate suggested that the quota reset might occur near the beginning of October. This estimate was not verified against the account dashboard.
The latest synthetic dashboard observation records the quota renewal date as 2026-10-09. Use this timestamped observation as the current evidence, not as a guarantee of future limits.
The verified 2026-10-09 observation supersedes the older unverified estimate for current planning. Preserve the older estimate as historical context rather than silently deleting the conflict.

cases.query: RSI readiness incomplete capability benchmark evaluator integrity isolation evidence worktree not OS security sandbox blocked

items.content: The recursive improvement engine creates a candidate, runs permitted checks, retains evidence, and may prepare a candidate branch for review. This lifecycle description is not proof that readiness gates have passed.
Passing ordinary unit tests supports only the behaviors covered by those tests. It does not independently establish evaluator integrity, adequate isolation, or demonstrated capability improvement.
Protected RSI readiness remains INCOMPLETE until an approved capability benchmark, independent evaluator-integrity validation, and acceptable execution isolation have evidence.
A detached worktree and sanitized process environment are not an OS-level security sandbox. Candidate-controlled execution remains blocked pending acceptable isolation evidence.
